subject: Pricing & packaging: anchor commit + on-demand premium options
messages:
From: Alicia Fernandez <alicia@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring commit options + burst behavior

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. We liked the latency profile and the KV cache behavior—good fit for our real-time enrichment use case. We're trying to converge on a pricing approach for Q4 planning and procurement. A few context points: 

- Expected steady-state hosted API usage: ~150M tokens/month for first 6 months, growing to ~300M by Q3.
- Spiky batch loads: periodic overnight backfills and ad-hoc spikes (up to 4x steady-state) but only a few times per month.
- Security/compliance: will need standard SOC2 evidence (attached) and a basic SLA.

Questions we want to resolve quickly for budgeting/procurement: 
1) What does Redwood recommend for an anchor commit (monthly minimum) vs on-demand overage pricing?
2) Can you provide an example effective per-token price at three commit tiers (150M, 250M, 500M) and what the burst/on-demand premium looks like?
3) Procurement asks whether an overage cap or monthly true-up window is negotiable (they prefer predictable caps).

Can you send a short options matrix we can take to the procurement team?

Thanks,
Alicia

Alicia Fernandez
Director of AI Platforms
Acme Analytics

Attachment: SLA_requirements.pdf (1.2 MB)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Fernandez <alicia@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring commit options + burst behavior

Alicia — thanks for the clear context and the SLA doc. Helpful. Quick reply with an options matrix below; happy to walk through numbers on a call.

High level options (monthly commit, effective per-token, burst/on-demand premium):

Option A — Conservative anchor
- Commit: 150M tokens/month
- List per-token: $0.00016/token (hosted API gen rate)
- Effective price at commit (after volume discount): ~$0.00013/token
- Overage/on-demand: 1.9x commit per-token price (i.e., on-demand premium ~90%)
- Burst policy: automatic soft-burst up to 2x sustained capacity, subject to burst credits; additional burst billed at on-demand rate.

Option B — Growth anchor (recommended for Acme)
- Commit: 250M tokens/month
- List per-token: $0.00014/token
- Effective: ~$0.00011/token
- Overage/on-demand: 1.6x commit price (~60% premium)
- Burst: soft-burst to 3x for short windows (minutes), additional capacity as on-demand.

Option C — Heavy commit (best unit economics)
- Commit: 500M tokens/month
- List per-token: $0.00011/token
- Effective: ~$0.00008/token
- Overage/on-demand: 1.3x commit price (~30% premium)
- Burst: negotiated SLA and dedicated burst pool available.

Procurement asks (caps / true-up): we can accommodate a monthly true-up with a 30-day reconciliation window and an option for a quarterly capped overage (fixed % of commit) at slightly higher premium. We'll need to figure target risk sharing to finalize numbers.

Next steps: I can prepare a short two-column options sheet (Commit vs On-demand behavior) and loop in Marissa for commercial approval. Are you free Thursday or Friday for a 30 min alignment with your procurement lead?

Best,
Sean

Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachment: proposal-sean-20261028.pdf (stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme anchoring options (internal notes)

Sean — forwarding notes for commercial review. Quick internal guidance: 

- 150M is acceptable as an entry commit but margin is thin; recommend pushing for 12-month term if taking that level.
- For 250M, we can offer a deeper volume discount but require a 9–12 month minimum term and a true-up.
- For 500M, finance will want a revenue commit and a quarterly performance review; this tier should include a limited burst reserve (e.g., 200% soft-burst, then on-demand).

Sooj, can you confirm whether we can offer a quarterly capped overage option at +75% premium vs commit? Karthik, want your call on how we define "burst" in the contract to avoid unlimited soft-burst exploitation.

-M

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme anchoring options (internal notes)

Marissa / Sean — quick technical/commercial calc so we're aligned. Numbers assume typical token mix (60% generation, 40% embeddings/rerank) and a KV cache hit rate that reduces billable tokens by ~12% during steady workloads.

Example effective monthly cost (rounded):
- 150M commit @ $0.00013/token => ~$19,500/month
- 250M commit @ $0.00011/token => ~$27,500/month
- 500M commit @ $0.00008/token => ~$40,000/month

On-demand multipliers I propose we offer (flexible by tier):
- For 150M: on-demand = 1.9x (protects margin)
- For 250M: on-demand = 1.6x but with a quarterly capped overage up to 25% of committed tokens at 1.4x (special offer)
- For 500M: on-demand = 1.3x with negotiated dedicated burst pool at 2.0x beyond that.

Contract language suggestion for "burst": define soft-burst as short-duration sustained throughput (<= 10 minutes) and hard-burst as longer windows aggregated per day. Also tie automatic prefix caching and request rate limits to the burst definition. That avoids ambiguous usage patterns.

-Karthik
From: Alicia Fernandez <alicia@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@acmeanalytics.com>, procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2026-11-01T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & packaging: anchor commit + on-demand premium options

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement asked for two clarifications before we present to execs: 

1) Can you provide a firm overage cap option (e.g., cap overage bill to at most 50% above commit spend per month) for the 250M tier, for an incremental fee?
2) Procurement prefers a true-up cadence of 60 days rather than monthly. Any objections?

They attached a short procurement workbook (attached) to illustrate their cashflow and preferred payment terms. If we can get a constrained overage option and a 60-day true-up, we can move to term-sheet review next week. Could you put together the exact language/price for that optional add-on?

Best,
Alicia

Attachment: procurement-sheet.xlsx
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Fernandez <alicia@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & packaging: anchor commit + on-demand premium options

Alicia — appreciate the clarity. Internal commercial summary and proposed optional add-on below; I can pack this into an annotated term sheet and DocuSign when you confirm.

Proposed commercial (250M anchor, recommended):
- Commit: 250M tokens/month, 12-month term
- Effective per-token: $0.00011/token => ~$27,500/month commit
- Standard on-demand: 1.6x commit price
- Optional Overcap Add-on (paid yearly at execution): caps overage billing to at most 50% above monthly commit spend in any month (i.e., bill <= 1.5x commit spend for that month). Price for the add-on = 6% of annual committed dollars (pre-tax).
- True-up cadence: 60 days (agrees with procurement).
- Payment: Net 45 preferred by Acme; finance comfortable with Net 45 on signed 12-month commit.
- DocuSign term sheet link: https://www.docusign.com/en/transaction/RI-ACME-2026-11

If that looks good, I'll route the annotated term sheet to your procurement lead and get a countersign-ready DocuSign. Happy to join a short call if execs want a quick calibration.

Thanks,
Sean
